title: Binary Prefix-Then-Copy Machine
statement: For each finite Boolean word $w$, there is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with no work tapes and $|w|+1$ states, initially in state $0$. In any state $q$ with $q<|w|$, it stays on the input cell, outputs the $q$th bit of $w$, and advances to state $q+1$. In any state $q$ with $q\ge |w|$, it moves right and outputs the scanned input bit while that bit is present, remaining in state $q$; on a blank cell it stays in place, outputs nothing, and halts.
